batch_strategy: Supplement the pending 16 with matched protocol comparisons, targeted tests of endpoint-specific loading response, and checks of unusual interval predictions. Use all supplied premeasurement predictions unchanged; freeze these 16 choices together with the pending 16 before any label reveal.

choices.reason: Measure m177 at 20/1 and 50 uL, predicted 6.62/49.09 mL. At 50/1, measured 5b706e17e8412d02342f and b514312eda7950cdcf1c changed from 21.33/59.88 to 4.49/81.30 as sample volume increased from 50 to 150 uL. The 20/1 high-load reference 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7 is 4.78/57.02. This tests whether the pronounced widening with amount persists at a stronger mobile phase or is confined to 50/1.

Measure m125 at 2/1, 150 uL sample and 300 uL DCM, predicted 29.86/62.68. Measured facbcedbecb46072b04c is 32.95/69.81 with 500 uL DCM. The completed 5/1 comparison revealed a large loading-volume-associated onset difference at high amount. This matched high-amount comparison tests whether that difference transfers across mobile-phase strength.

Pair the preceding m125 experiment with 2/1, 50 uL sample and 300 uL DCM, predicted 29.89/62.64. At 5/1 and fixed 300-uL DCM volume, measured 780b13846ace50ede763 and 549daca56bed1c9d2bcc have identical onsets despite a threefold amount change. This pair tests the amount response at 2/1 without changing the recorded loading protocol.

Measure the m125 5/1 midpoint at 100 uL sample in 300 uL DCM, predicted 36.66/67.38. Both measured endpoints of this amount series, 780b13846ace50ede763 and 549daca56bed1c9d2bcc, start at 42.27 mL, whereas the current midpoint prediction starts substantially earlier. This discriminates a flat onset response from a local nonmonotonic response or record variability and prevents importing the 500-uL protocol's loading slope indiscriminately.

Measure m72 at 10/1, 150 uL sample in 300 uL PE, predicted 13.35/31.99. At 20/1, measured 8e7636d7a60a6058305a and 754f1d33b0ed61557754 show earlier onset at higher amount under this PE protocol. Paired with the selected DCM experiment, this tests whether the protocol difference and amount sensitivity persist near the much shorter predicted 10/1 interval.

Measure m72 at 10/1, 150 uL sample in 200 uL DCM, predicted 13.27/32.10. This matches the selected PE experiment in molecule, amount and mobile phase; loading solvent and loading volume change together. Measured 7383949c431e18f39597 provides the 50-uL DCM reference at 12.85/32.50. The pair tests the model's near-invariance to protocol and supplies a within-DCM amount contrast.

Measure methyl mandelate m99 at 5/1 and 50 uL, predicted 18.43/29.68. Measured 12ab195583f05b9aa177 at 100 uL is 19.91/32.37, while d8fcb58722028dbf9c02, c61c1a72306f2ee37df8 and 7bbdec21c428010dd67b establish a decreasing onset across 50–150 uL at 10/1. This tests attenuation or reversal of that response at stronger elution strength under the same 1000-uL DCM protocol.

Measure meta-aminobenzonitrile m161 at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 28.52/78.20. Measured a60552f4d1a5ced4641f and 3774a4dac6dd0f01d48d give 34.93/86.44 and 25.20/80.63 at 50 and 150 uL. The current completion prediction lies below both measured endpoints. The midpoint distinguishes smooth amount dependence from a local minimum and constrains both endpoints in a recently mispredicted basic polar family.

Measure m37 at 10/1 and 150 uL, predicted 26.16/48.93. The matched low-amount observation 9ae9c8b491a04e429a11 is 28.69/54.81. At 20/1, 606886b17304ec494aa0, b6f1b33a5491968c645e and 3b2c663a28a9f32bd1d3 show a substantial onset decrease with nearly stable completion. This tests whether stronger elution changes which endpoint responds to loading.

Measure methyl acetoacetate m95 at 50/1 and 100 uL, predicted 23.70/71.85. The high-amount observation 5fd0921bbbba1e22abf9 is 18.45/75.76 and previously exposed a large completion underestimate. Together with the available 10/1 observations, this probes loading and solvent response in an aliphatic beta-ketoester, testing transfer beyond aromatic alcohols and nitrogen-containing compounds.

Measure cyano-substituted benzophenone m159 at 50/1 and 150 uL, predicted 53.85/106.09. Measured a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 at 100 uL is 57.88/117.93; a738b1f204da6fcfd385 and 79ff49052bce33597828 anchor its shorter 20/1 and 10/1 intervals. This tests whether the model's lower completion is a real amount response and whether the unusual nitrobenzophenone response transfers to another polar benzophenone topology.

Measure nitrophenethyl alcohol m200 at 2/1 and 150 uL, predicted 31.30/69.41, against measured low-amount a92f7617b135de150588 at 33.88/74.44. The 1/1 reference 97318de99bab4460cf4e anchors the solvent curve. This extends amount-response learning to combined alcohol/nitro functionality and tests whether both endpoints shift, unlike several nearly completion-invariant families.

Measure diethyl phenylmalonate m75 at 2/1 and 100 uL, predicted 10.07/12.21. Recent low-amount f2312f90dd4cf5ef0e23 measured an almost collapsed interval, 12.58/12.61, while d4d7270df69266029f44 at 1/1 and f82f2844c7e27afd32b1e at 5/1 give ordinary intervals at 100 uL. This tests whether the unusual 2/1 behavior extends to a neighboring amount or is an isolated record feature.

Introduce unmeasured para-chloroanisole m121 at 50/1 and 100 uL, predicted 6.79/11.24. Its maximum similarity to measured molecules is 0.6875. Measured b1737f3e487bbd039406 and 4a49effd313865c10fae anchor anisole, and 18f616a941bed3e03c3f anchors para-bromoanisole at 50/1 under a different loading protocol. This supplies a structural-transfer test in the common early-eluting aromatic region, outside the retained polar families.

Measure para-iodophenol m208 at 50/1 and 150 uL, predicted 28.72/62.85. Measured 0b8c6c59ae5e24b420e5 gives 26.27/49.10 at 20/1 and 100 uL; the pending 5/1 high-amount experiment provides a prospective same-amount solvent contrast. This tests the weak-mobile-phase extension of phenol retention and endpoint response, with potential transfer to the other phenolic rows.

Measure long-chain dibromothiophene m71 in pure EA at 150 uL, for which the predictor gives reversed endpoints, 8.51/7.70. Measured bd62986a3ea6d28161ec at 1/1 and e9aa21d2af3158cfa4f5 at 10/1 show ordinary early-eluting intervals. This checks an uncovered strong-solvent regime for an unusual hydrophobic topology and provides a concrete endpoint-consistency correction; the reversal is model behavior, not a measured property.

hypotheses.content: Increasing sample amount often advances onset more than completion, but the magnitude and endpoint balance depend on molecular connectivity and mobile-phase strength. A universal loading correction is unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many current predictions remain almost invariant to amount. Cross-condition contrasts can teach when endpoint-specific loading effects are substantial and when they are small, improving transfer across the numerous condition variants in the catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m99 and m37 show weaker or qualitatively different amount responses under stronger mobile phases, and do m161, m95 and m200 follow the predicted endpoint trends?

hypotheses.content: The apparent loading response is protocol-dependent in m125 and m72, but the recorded comparisons do not yet distinguish reproducible interactions from record variability. In particular, m125's onset decrease with amount at 500 uL DCM does not occur at the measured endpoints using 300 uL DCM.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The current predictor gives nearly identical predictions across protocols despite substantial observed differences in selected regimes. Attributing all of these differences to sample amount would teach an incorrect general rule. The m125 comparisons isolate loading volume, whereas m72 comparisons change solvent identity and loading volume together.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m125 loading-volume contrast recur at 2/1, does its 300-uL DCM amount midpoint preserve the equal endpoint onsets at 5/1, and does the m72 protocol difference persist at 10/1?

hypotheses.content: The early-onset, late-completion pattern of nitrobenzophenone m177 is strongly amount-dependent at 50/1 in the supplied observations. Its interval widens through both earlier onset and later completion, unlike the mostly onset-driven response of nitroacetophenone m37.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A broad tail correction or a topology-independent loading slope cannot represent these different endpoint responses. The evidence supports an association from two m177 amounts, without identifying an adsorption mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does lower loading at 20/1 also delay m177 onset and shorten completion, and does cyano-benzophenone m159 exhibit a comparable response in its weak-solvent regime?

hypotheses.content: Nearly collapsed or reversed measured intervals may be localized record features rather than general retention-response rules. Neighboring amount labels are needed before the model spreads these patterns across a solvent curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m195 low- and middle-amount records now agree much better with each other than with the reversed high-amount record. A new nearly collapsed m75 interval raises the same learning risk, but does not establish a shared cause or justify rejecting any label.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m75 at 2/1 and 100 uL retain the nearly collapsed interval observed at 50 uL, or return to an ordinary interval consistent with its neighboring solvent conditions?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measurements strengthen endpoint-specific loading effects without supporting a universal slope. The m141 and m204 midpoints lie between their low- and high-amount onsets, and the completed m99 series decreases from 44.43 to 38.99 to 34.78 mL in onset while completion changes much less. The m37 high-amount result continues its onset trend. The aminobenzonitrile isomers also elute earlier at higher amount, with a larger onset change for the meta isomer. However, m128 at 5/1 and m119 at 2/1 show relatively modest onset changes. The most consequential revision concerns m125: at 300 uL DCM, its two measured amount endpoints have exactly the same onset, whereas the 500-uL protocol shows a substantial decrease. This weakens an amount-only interpretation and motivates explicit protocol comparisons. For m72, the new low-amount PE result supports both an amount association within PE and a protocol-associated difference from DCM, with solvent identity and loading volume still confounded. The two new m173 results agree closely with the alternative protocol at 2/1 and 5/1, weakening a broad loading-volume explanation for its exceptional 1/1 completion discrepancy; I therefore do not add more m173 rows now. The m177 low-amount outcome rejects the tentative expectation that its extremely early onset would persist unchanged: onset was much later and completion earlier than predicted. The m195 low-amount result agrees with its 100-uL neighbor and leaves the reversed 150-uL interval isolated. Pending-CW feedback adds the nearly collapsed m75 2/1 interval and the ordinary 1/1 result, motivating one neighboring check. These are acquisition-time errors and measured contrasts, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The pending batch already covers several routine solvent-response regions, phenol and alcohol conditions, and a strong-solvent m72 point. The supplements concentrate on relationships for which the latest labels changed the scientific interpretation: three m125 experiments distinguish amount, loading volume and solvent-regime effects; two matched m72 experiments test whether its protocol difference persists away from 20/1; and the m177 experiment tests a newly demonstrated change in both endpoints. Further amount contrasts span an alpha-hydroxy ester, a beta-ketoester, aminobenzonitrile, nitroketone, cyano-benzophenone and nitroalcohol, providing independent tests of whether the model can learn conditional loading effects. The m75 neighbor constrains how broadly an unusual measured interval should influence predictions. Para-chloroanisole adds useful structural transfer in the common early-eluting region, m208 extends a solvent curve jointly with a pending experiment, and m71 tests an uncovered regime with an explicit endpoint-order failure. The batch favors contrasts that can discriminate explanations over additional labels around already resolved curves. Quantile spreads are treated as single-predictor diagnostics, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and interval width is treated as a chromatographic outcome. The expected benefit is better structure-condition-endpoint prediction across the Row-distribution; no chromatographic performance objective or new labels were used to choose the batch.
